source_name: IFC Project Disclosure Portal (Summary of Investment Information / ESRS)
why_relevant: IFC must disclose an SII for each investment; filtering by country=Montenegro and sector=financial institutions surfaces bank clients, their sponsors and governance/E&S conditions, including corporate-governance improvement plans that drive board and organisational change.

source_name: World Bank Group Finances One — IFC investment services project datasets
why_relevant: Machine-readable IFC/WBG project datasets allow systematic extraction of Montenegro financial-sector counterparties over time without scraping the HTML portal — a good backbone for entity/actor mapping.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations — Montenegro (incl. Financial Sector PBG, P167665)
why_relevant: Programme documents and implementation reports for Montenegro's financial-sector operations describe reform of supervisory institutions, deposit protection and consumer protection — i.e. mandated organisational change in the CBCG and peers.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro Report 2025 (SWD(2025) 754 final)
why_relevant: The annual enlargement report assesses Chapter 9 (financial services) and Chapter 4 alignment, the administrative and staffing capacity of the CBCG and supervisory agencies, and flags appointment/independence issues — the authoritative outside account of organisational change in Montenegrin financial institutions.

source_name: European Parliament report on the Commission reports on Montenegro (A10-0093/2025)
why_relevant: EP rapporteur reports comment on politicised appointments and institutional independence, often naming contested leadership processes at regulators — a complementary, more explicit political read than the Commission's SWD.

source_name: EU.me — Montenegro's accession negotiation portal, Chapter 9 Financial Services
why_relevant: Montenegro's own EU-facing portal publishes chapter negotiating structures, working-group composition and benchmark progress in both Montenegrin and English — working-group membership is a direct list of named officials in financial-sector institutions.

source_name: EEAS — EU Delegation to Montenegro, press and project pages
why_relevant: The Delegation announces EU-funded financial-sector programmes with EBRD and partner banks and hosts bilingual (EN/ME) press releases naming institutional counterparts and programme leads.

source_name: IMF — Montenegro country page and Article IV staff reports
why_relevant: Article IV reports and concluding statements explicitly address CBCG operational independence and whether it is 'appropriately staffed' — a direct, dated external signal on hiring/organisational capacity at the central bank, plus banking-sector structure commentary.

source_name: IMF Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) — Montenegro
why_relevant: FSAP reports profile supervisory organisation, staffing and governance arrangements of the CBCG in depth; infrequent but the most granular external description of the supervisor's internal structure.

source_name: CBCG — EU projects / international technical cooperation pages
why_relevant: The central bank's own EU-facing English/Montenegrin pages list twinning and IPA projects, resident twinning advisers and beneficiary departments — mapping which CBCG units are being reorganised and who leads them.

source_name: Twinning partner central banks/supervisors publishing on Montenegro (HNB, Deutsche Bundesbank, BaFin, DNB, HANFA)
why_relevant: Twinning partners publish their own project accounts naming the beneficiary departments, the resident twinning adviser and CBCG counterparts — an external mirror of CBCG organisational reform that local sources often omit.

source_name: BIS central bankers' speeches archive
why_relevant: BIS republishes speeches by CBCG governors and by foreign officials speaking about Montenegro in English; the by-line itself is a reliable, dated confirmation of who holds which office.

source_name: NLB Group investor-relations / Addiko takeover disclosure pages
why_relevant: English-language takeover documentation for Addiko Bank AG covers the Montenegrin subsidiary's fate (carve-out/sale), the strongest current driver of ownership, management and organisational change in Montenegro's banking market.

source_name: Addiko Bank AG group investor relations / ad-hoc disclosures
why_relevant: Parent-level ad-hoc releases and annual reports disclose management-board changes, country-CEO appointments and the planned separation of the Montenegrin unit — the primary English record for Addiko banka AD Podgorica leadership.

source_name: SeeNews — South-East Europe business newswire
why_relevant: The main English-language regional wire covering Montenegrin bank M&A, rating actions and executive appointments; often the first English record of a management change reported locally in Montenegrin.

source_name: European Western Balkans — accession-monitoring analysis in English
why_relevant: Specialist English outlet that distils each enlargement report and follows appointment/independence controversies at Montenegrin institutions faster than the official documents themselves.

source_name: Cbonds issuer profiles for Montenegrin banks (e.g. Hipotekarna banka)
why_relevant: Aggregates issuer identifiers (LEI, SWIFT), rating history and news for Montenegrin banks in English — useful for entity resolution across IFI, rating and press sources, and for spotting rating actions that discuss management quality.

source_name: TheBanks.eu — Montenegro bank profiles (management, ownership, market share)
why_relevant: Maintains English profiles of every licensed Montenegrin bank including ownership, market share and board composition — a convenient cross-check layer for the actor map, though derived rather than primary.

source_name: Fitch Ratings / Moody's / S&P / Scope — Montenegro sovereign and bank rating pages
why_relevant: Rating agencies publish rating-action commentaries that assess governance, management quality and ownership change; sovereign actions on Montenegro are free, and agency coverage of parent groups (OTP, Erste, NLB, RBI) reaches the Montenegrin subsidiaries.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking trade portal, EBRD tag
why_relevant: Specialist Montenegrin banking outlet with a dedicated tag stream for EBRD ('Evropska banka za obnovu i razvoj'); the local-language mirror of the international layer and a strong pointer to which IFI deals and executive appointments matter domestically.

source_name: ecoi.net — archived copies of EU/IFI country documents on Montenegro
why_relevant: Stable third-party archive of enlargement reports and related institutional documents, useful when EC URLs rotate between publication cycles and for building a longitudinal series of institutional-capacity assessments.

source_name: SeeNews — Montenegro Company News
why_relevant: SeeNews is the reference SEE business wire and runs a dedicated Montenegro 'Company News' stream that carries CEO appointments, board changes, rebrandings and M&A for Montenegrin corporates and banks (observed items: Nova Banka->Adriatic Bank rename, Porto Montenegro CEO, EPCG/CGES CEO, EBRD Montenegro head). Its regional beat routinely publishes subsidiary leadership news in English before Montenegrin outlets are picked up internationally.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — Montenegro / Western Balkans banking coverage
why_relevant: Emerging-markets wire with sustained Montenegrin banking coverage: bank exits, ownership changes and consolidation (observed: Societe Generale exit/merge in Montenegro; Serbian company bidding for Prva Banka). Useful for M&A-driven reorganisation signals framed regionally, and for cross-border owner moves that precede local management changes.

source_name: Biznis.rs — 'Region' section (Serbian business portal)
source_subtype: national business news portal, regional desk
why_relevant: Serbian business daily portal with an explicit 'Region' desk that covers Montenegrin bank ownership and management news in Serbian (observed: 'Kompanija Aleksandra Kostića kupuje crnogorsku Hipotekarnu banku'). Also covers Serbian parent-bank executive appointments (Komercijalna banka izvršni odbor) that determine Montenegrin subsidiary leadership.

source_name: Bloomberg Adria (Serbian edition) — Biznis/Kompanije
why_relevant: The flagship pan-Adriatic financial newsroom (RS/HR/SI editions) built specifically for the ex-Yugoslav market; covers AIK/Agri Europe group deals and bank ownership transfers in Serbian (observed: 'AIK i zvanično vlasnik Eurobank Direktne'). Highest-value regional channel for M&A-driven reorganisation affecting Montenegrin subsidiaries.

source_name: B92 Biz — Region
why_relevant: Serbian mainstream portal with a business 'Region' feed that ran an explicitly structural piece on Montenegro's bank market ('Preuzimanja, novi igrači: Bankarska scena Crne Gore dobija novi oblik'). Useful for takeover/new-entrant framing and for cheap, freely accessible Serbian-language monitoring of Montenegrin bank restructuring.

source_name: Poslovni dnevnik — Montenegro edition (Crna Gora desk)
why_relevant: Croatian business daily brand operating a Montenegro-facing edition; observed deal reporting 'Kostićev Agri Europe Cyprus preuzima Hipotekarnu banku za 75 milijuna eura'. Croatian-inflected regional business press is a distinct channel from Montenegrin outlets and often carries deal mechanics and integration detail.
